adaptations: fixed corpus pool replaces generated sibling candidates
Node.code uses a real candidate filename as an identity stub; original code-text equality across different candidate IDs is not modeled
saved author judgments replace API responses; identity remapped before parser
missing confidence uses original parser fallback 0.5
serial comparisons for deterministic ordering; original tournament unchanged
actual candidate execution replaced by reading stored utility after selection
pool_sampling: Candidates require finite recorded scores for evaluability (one Google Quest NaN candidate excluded); no ranking or score magnitude is used for pool construction. Seeded shuffled greedy complete subgraphs; target min(10, eligible task candidates). If 500 construction trials fail target, enumerate maximal cliques to find largest feasible size <=10. Each pool gets up to 5000 trials; fallback uniform choice among feasible maximal cliques, then uniform subset. Selection depends only on candidate identity and pair coverage.

metrics.primary: Uniform-tie best-hit = number of optimal pool candidates in rank-0 set / set size. This analytically averages a uniform choice within the tied top group; it is a tie-adjusted diagnostic, not a change to original multi-candidate execution.
metrics.random_reference: Uniform single candidate in same pool; best-hit = optimal_count / pool_size.
metrics.percentile: Mean over rank-0 candidates of (number strictly worse + 0.5*other equal)/ (n-1); higher better.
metrics.regret: (best pool utility - mean rank-0 utility)/(best-worst pool utility); lower better.
metrics.aggregation: Average repeats within pool, pools within task, then 26 tasks equally. Overlapping pools and repeated feedback are dependent; descriptive results only.
metrics.execution: For every rank-0 candidate independently call original should_execute() at p=.2. Log actual simulated selected identities, empty rate and best-executed hit; also report exact expectations conditional on top group.
